newsitem.title: HAITI: Haiti lawmakers give Smarth vote of confidence.
newsitem.headline: Haiti lawmakers give Smarth vote of confidence.

text.p: Haitian Prime Minister Rosny Smarth survived a confidence vote on Thursday after a raucous 15-hour session in which lawmakers threatened to oust him and questioned the government's economic recovery plan.
With a majority vote needed to remove the prime minister under the Haitian constitution, 37 deputies voted for Smarth, 29 against, and six abstained.
"The government will stay in place, but it is not because we are convinced," Deputy Gabriel Fortune said after the votes were counted at 3 a.m. Thursday.
"We want to give them a chance, given that it would be disruptive to bring in a whole new team," he added.

Smarth has been the target of vigorous public opposition. In a series of general strikes and demonstrations, popular organisations have protested against the government's economic plan, which calls for privatisation of nine state enterprises, including the telephone and electricity companies.
Many deputies expressed dissatisfaction with the economic plan. But those who supported Smarth noted that it had been approved by the lower chamber, albeit by a narrow majority.
At the start of the session on Wednesday, members of grassroots organisations clashed with Smarth supporters outside the parliament building.
A fight broke out, and police prevented an anti-government demonstrator from putting a tire around an opponent's head.
"Despite our vote, I believe the popular organisations in the street will eventually force Smarth out," Fortune said.
